claims.text: Atomic-scale lattice distortions in a chemically disordered HEA matrix interact with dislocations during high-strain-rate loading.
The interaction between lattice distortions and dislocations activates additional slip systems.
The interaction between lattice distortions and dislocations promotes dynamic strain aging.
Additional slip-system activation and dynamic strain aging enable HEAs to exhibit high strength and ductility simultaneously.
The target HEA has a single-phase, chemically disordered, uniform solid-solution microstructure.
Atomic-scale lattice distortions arise from high configurational entropy.
Local solute inhomogeneities produce atomic-scale lattice distortions.
Under high-strain-rate loading, the locally distorted lattice enhances dislocation interactions.
Enhanced dislocation interactions limit dislocation pile-up.
Enhanced dislocation interactions promote dynamic recovery.
Limiting dislocation pile-up and promoting dynamic recovery underpin increased strength and ductility.
Under high-strain-rate loading, the HEA will activate more slip systems than the conventional-alloy baseline.
Under high-strain-rate loading, the HEA will show more evidence of dynamic strain aging than the conventional-alloy baseline.
The HEA will have greater dynamic ductility than the conventional-alloy baseline.
The HEA will have greater dynamic strength than the conventional-alloy baseline.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply to HEAs that retain a single-phase solid solution.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when significant secondary phases form.
The proposed mechanism may not apply in temperature or strain-rate regimes where thermal activation dominates deformation.
The magnitude of additional slip-system activation and the quantitative relationship between lattice distortion and dynamic strain aging are not precisely established.
